deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck studies finite systems of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. Here, as on neighbouring pages, P^2(R) is drawn as a disc with antipodal boundary points identified. The boundary circle represents one distinguished pseudo-line, the line at infinity, traversed twice. The orange curves are the other pseudo-lines.

The boundary carries the following marks:
- u and u' are antipodal boundary points, i.e. one point of the line at infinity.
- Black arcs alpha, beta and gamma are drawn on the boundary.
- Green dots split the boundary into stretches marked '1/2', which looks like a normalised length.

The black arcs appear to be 'arcs of specialization': intervals on the distinguished line along which a point, or the end of an added pseudo-line, can be moved to specialise the configuration. That would mean making it pass through a multiple point, i.e. degenerating the arrangement.

The central figure is a smaller example. It shows a near-symmetric star-like arrangement with green boundary arcs, some dashed.

Left figure. s and t are two multiple points. The NB assumes there is at least one pseudo-line not passing through s or t. This excludes the degenerate family III_{p,q} (p,q >= 1): p lines through s, q lines through t, plus presumably the line st, a 'double pencil'. The claim is that when exactly one pseudo-line avoids s and t, every exceptional specialization arc gamma has length 0, i.e. degenerates to a point.

Right figure. The analogous statement for a single multiple point u = u'. The trivial case I_n is the pencil, all n lines through one point. Assume at least one pseudo-line avoids u. If exactly one does (a near-pencil), the exceptional specialization arc gamma has length 0.

Bottom strip diagrams. These show the Möbius band cut open along a transversal (vertical dashed lines mark the gluing, with the twist). Orange bundles are crossing pseudo-lines near multiple points. The green/black/dashed curve is a pseudo-line being moved: it crosses from one side of the strip to the other and passes through the multiple point u = u'. Hatched grey regions are the cells it sweeps.

The page thus records a case analysis for the exceptional specialization arcs of an arrangement relative to one or two multiple points. The arcs and lengths look like part of a combinatorial or metric description of the space of one-element extensions of a pseudo-line arrangement, i.e. of its degenerations.
errors: The '1/2' normalisation is never defined on this page. The claims that gamma has length 0 in the extremal cases cannot be checked without the definition from earlier pages. They are plausible: in a near-pencil there are too few vertices for a nondegenerate arc to exist.
'dans tous les cas Str_3 [?] non plus' is unclear in the image. The exact list of excluded configurations is uncertain.

ideas.what: Classification of degenerate arrangements: pencil I_n and double pencils III_{p,q} through two points s,t
ideas.modern_name: pencils / near-pencils / arrangements with few vertices (Sylvester-Gallai-type extremal configurations)

ideas.what: Arcs of (exceptional) specialization along a distinguished pseudo-line, with normalised lengths, controlling how an arrangement degenerates or extends
ideas.modern_name: one-element extensions / extension space of rank-3 oriented matroids; mutations (triangle flips) and the cell structure of the space of arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (extensions, 1978), Sturmfels-Ziegler (extension spaces, 1993), Ringel (mutation graph 1956), Goodman-Pollack

ideas.what: Strip (cut-open Möbius band) picture of a pseudo-line being moved through a multiple point
ideas.modern_name: wiring diagrams / allowable sequences; local triangle-flip move

missed.claim: Grothendieck seems to equip the boundary (the line at infinity) with a normalised metric. In it, the specialization arcs of an arrangement relative to its multiple points have lengths, and in extremal cases (near-pencil, near double pencil) the exceptional arc degenerates to length 0. This metric or length structure on extension or specialization loci has no clear counterpart in the oriented-matroid extension-space literature, which is purely combinatorial.
missed.quote: Dans le cas où il n'y en a qu'une, l'arc de spécialisation exceptionnel γ est de longueur 0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may be a fragment of a canonical geometric (Teichmüller-like) model of the moduli of pseudo-line arrangements, a theme Grothendieck's tame-topology programme hints at. Its exact content is unclear from this page alone.

deep.surprise_reason: These are typical working notes on pseudo-line arrangements and their degenerations. The objects (pencils, near-pencils, flips) are classical. The only distinctive element is the length-normalised specialization arcs, whose meaning cannot be fully pinned down from this page.
